sections.content: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the skeleton of every web page. It describes structure using tags — headings, paragraphs, links, images — that browsers render.
HTML is not a programming language; it has no variables or logic. It is a markup language: you describe WHAT things are, and CSS handles how they look.
Key points: every page is a tree of nested elements, tags usually come in open/close pairs, and browsers are forgiving but you should write correct HTML.
